There's nothing inherently bad about using Java, but it might not be what most people prefer to use. It depends on your goal. If you're programing for fun, then do what you want to do. If your intent is to become a well-rounded programmer, perhaps you should experiment with different paradigms.

Depends what you're making. Java is good if you need to include hundreds of external dependencies/libraries. C is good if you want something fast or lightweight. Python is fast to code with, but relatively slow to execute. Eventually a favourite will emerge depending on what you do.

Totally depends on your goals. Java is an interpreted language, so speed is not it's strong point. It runs on just about anything though...at the end of the day it's upto you, try different things out and you'll get a feeling for a languages strengths and weaknesses...

Java is an interpreted language

Java is compiled. You might be thinking of JavaScript, which is interpreted.

Ya got me on a technicality. Apologies... Java is a compiled programming language, but rather than compile straight to executable machine code, it compiles to an intermediate binary form called JVM byte code. The byte code is then compiled and/or interpreted to run the program.
It is 100% dependent on what you are trying to make. Java is fine for many things. C is fine for many things. C++ as well. You don't have to pick just one language to use for everything.

My preference would be C++. But this mostly from my favoring of Mac and the Mac way. Most of us Mac users hate Java apps (even when it's supposed to be "native-like" it's still doesn't have that same feeling), and more and more of us Mac guys are refusing to install the JRE.

C++ offers great cross-platform capability, while still offering options for Native-like cross-platforming, or, with only a bit of native code on top of a common codebase, offer a truly native experience on the major platforms.

Then, C++ is a bit more flexible than Java. Anywhere Java can be used, C++ can be used, but Java can't be used anywhere C++ is used. For example, while Java has some very nice game engines, there's not really anything that compares to Unreal. Generally, Java and C++ are great at handling complexity, but C++ is going to pull ahead when great efficiency is needed. There's some other applications where C++ is going to generally be better, such as anything low level.

Java does have one major advantage: it's less demanding on you, the programmer. My way of making up for this is knowing multiple languages. C++ and Python make a great combination. Generally, knowing a general use higher level language (Python, Ruby, Javascript) and a general use "lower level" language (C, C++, D) will allow you to accomplish most tasks. If you want to focus on only one language, then I suppose somewhere between would do better (Java, C#).

C++ vs C? Coming from Java, you'll probably just want C++ for its OOP orientation. C has its appeal, though.

All said, you might just want to stick with Java and become a wizard at it. But don't be afraid to branch out too!

TL;DR: But yeah, unless you're wanting to work on a particular domain that heavily favoring one language, or your job demands a specific language, then it just comes down to personal preference and choosing a language which works well for the project.
